issue_title: Using a custom task_id on a chain results in an incomplete as_tuple graph.

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

```python from uuid import uuid4 from celery import Celery from celery import chain, group app = Celery("bug-example", backend="redis://localhost:6379/0", broker="amqp://guest:guest@localhost:5672//") @app.task(name="test1") def task1(): return None tasks_length = 5 worker_tasks = [ chain( app.signature("test1"), app.signature("test1") ) for i in range(tasks_length) ] post_processing_tasks = [] for i in range(tasks_length): t = [ task1.s(), task1.s(), task1.s(), task1.s(), ] post_processing_tasks.append(chain(*t)) tasks = [ task1.s(), group(worker_tasks), group(post_processing_tasks), task1.s(), task1.s(), ] last_task1 = chain(*tasks, task_id=str(uuid4())).apply_async() last_task2 = chain(*tasks, task_id="hello").apply_async() last_task3 = chain(*tasks).apply_async() print(last_task1.as_tuple()) print("------------------------------------------------------------------") print(last_task2.as_tuple()) print("------------------------------------------------------------------") print(last_task3.as_tuple()) ```
